gloss: boxed; packed in a box; sheltered; overprotected

definitions.explanation: describing an item that comes packaged in a box, typically implying higher quality or a gift presentation
describing a person, especially a young woman, who has been raised in a sheltered, protective environment with little exposure to the outside world

notes:
Literally "put in a box." The literal sense (sense 1) refers to items packaged in boxes, often implying quality or gift-readiness. The figurative sense (sense 2) describes someone raised in a protected environment, kept safe from the outside world like a treasured item in a box.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {箱入|はこい}り⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧: sheltered daughter — the most common figurative usage
- {箱入|はこい}り⟦{息子|むすこ}→息子：00799_musuko⟧: sheltered son — less common but used similarly
- {箱入|はこい}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧: boxed sweets

CULTURAL NOTE:
The expression {箱入|はこい}り⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧ traditionally described daughters from good families who were carefully protected from the outside world. In modern usage, it can carry either a positive nuance (well-bred, innocent) or a slightly critical one (naive, lacking worldly experience).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{世間知|せけんし}らず→世間知らず：22674_sekenshirazu⟧: naive about the world — focuses on the result of being sheltered
- ⟦お{嬢様|じょうさま}→お嬢様：23358_ojousama⟧⟦{育|そだ}ち→育ち：13927_sodachi⟧: raised like a young lady — similar connotation of privileged upbringing
